summary: The 42-class catalog is a finite combination of sensitive types and opaque carriers, not a complete inventory of personal attributes. Birth/demographic/belief fields have genuine catalog and direct-key gaps; existing phone/financial/location types also lack general value-shape detection. Select additions only after the separate real-corpus probe, and keep named hints distinct from actual observed value shapes.

possible_additions_not_approved_as_a_bat.minimal_value_evidence: Explicit direct key plus bounded calendar-date/year/partial-date shape. A date alone is not evidence of birth or linkage to a person. Preserve invalid dates and references as unknown.

Personal age field plus numeric/age-range syntax; no birth-date arithmetic or person profiling. Unqualified age can describe caches/objects, so require an explicit personal field definition or a qualified key.
Direct personal-attribute key and a nonempty value. Keep named-hint evidence; a finite enum is not complete and must not infer gender from names, pronouns or imagery.
Direct qualified field/value only; no racial inference from names, language, location or appearance. No claim that a text value reflects a real person.
Explicit field/value named hint, not a global religion-word dictionary. Do not infer belief from names, nationality, location or documents mentioning religions.
Explicit personal field and nonempty value; locality words alone cannot distinguish birth place from deployment region or a public place.
Direct qualified personal field only; country, locale and IP location do not establish nationality.
Explicit field/value or record carrier with personal linkage; institution names alone are not a personal education history.
Direct personal-record key; generic job/task/process/worker identifiers remain unrelated software terms.
Potential future direct-value hint, contingent on actual corpus evidence. Never infer political views from activity, identity or associations.
Potential future direct record hint, separate from current biometric template hints. DNA-like strings are not enough to identify a human genetic record.

The old local taxonomy explicitly lists SMS/email verification codes. Generic numeric strings/codes and references must not be treated as usable credentials; actual detection needs authentication context.

existing_type_detection_gaps.gap: Named hints exist; no current standalone phone/identity/card/account shape extractor. Any next finite syntax checker must keep context/example distinctions and never validate credential/account liveness.
latitude/longitude keys are recognized but generic number pairs are not location evidence; named hints currently perform no coordinate range or personal-linkage verification.
Only IPv4 currently has a literal checker; IPv6 and MAC-shaped forms remain unclassified without suitable names. They are possible finite stdlib/rule extensions, not universal person identifiers.
Keys supply hints; no general bare DB URI/DSN or path-privacy detector. URL userinfo is AUTH evidence and must not make every URL a database connection.

Not a free-text name recognizer; even middle_name/maiden_name aliases are absent, and username currently shares the person-name hint despite being potentially an account handle. Correcting existing username meaning is a separate migration decision from additive fields.

legacy_scope_conflicts.disposition: These belonged to a wider older scope. Current application-log v2 excludes Agent-native control/session objects. Generic source code may be public; generic timestamps are not personal. Do not silently reintroduce these as newly found sensitive data.

primary_sources.paraphrase: The list includes these and employment/education attributes when linked or linkable to an individual. This supports technical taxonomy terms, not claims that every matching token is personal or legally protected.

primary_sources.paraphrase: Age and gender can contribute to identification in combination with other information. This is contextual linkage, not standalone sensitive-word detection.

primary_sources.publication: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
primary_sources.paraphrase: Defines gender and birthdate as End-User claims; birthdate permits YYYY-MM-DD, omitted-year 0000, and year-only forms. It allows gender values beyond its two examples. Use as a field-format reference, not as identity or disclosure verification.

primary_sources.publication: Personal Data Categories 2.3, Final Community Group Report, 25 February 2026
primary_sources.section: Vocabulary index; Age, BirthDate, BirthPlace, Citizenship, Demographic, Ethnicity, Gender, Genetic, Education and EmploymentHistory terms
primary_sources.paraphrase: A primary vocabulary for personal-data categories; supports possible finer-grained labels. It is explicitly not a W3C Standard and is not used here to infer legal duties.
Defines a concept for information about a person’s religion or religious beliefs; field semantics still require context.
Distinguishes credentials, personal data, application code and commercially sensitive data from diagnostic event metadata. Used only as engineering scope guidance.
Explicitly includes SMS/email verification codes; no dedicated current one-time-code type or rule.
Mentions health and political inferences in an older Agent-native scope. Do not revive AGENT_DER or infer attributes automatically; current log-focused v2 takes precedence.

minimal_upgrade_sequence: Wait for the separately recorded real AIDev candidate-field probe; pick only a small justified subset and publish definitions/negative cases.

Keep six top-level categories and old subtype IDs; append approved PII subtype IDs with an explicit new taxonomy version (e.g. 1.1.0 for additive labels). Avoid adding new legacy coarse classes where personal_identifier is sufficient.
Expose key-only capability honestly; add contextual value-shape rules only when their parser and safe enum/cursor counterparts are actually implemented and synthetically verified.
After all sources freeze, run synthetic Git/PyDriller + plaintext/cursor + JSON/Parquet + mismatch-resume regressions and full suite.
Reclassify frozen source text into new independent run directories; do not mutate old outputs or label old annotations with the new version. Use current parent/repair pairs under the new guard.

Build a new version-aware inventory; preserve old 42-class evidence and mark newly introduced labels as not evaluated for old sources. Audit changed cell/type relationships, types, unknown queues and coverage separately.

implemented_upgrade_guard.behavior: Early locked validation rejects any parent or repair finite classifier that differs from installed content_types.py/taxonomy.py/storage.py, before metadata DB merge or creating output. Legacy and advance ancestry share this entry point.

failure_reproduced_before_fix.result: new-legacy genuine synthetic producers were incorrectly accepted; test failed DID NOT RAISE.

synthetic_gap_probe.result: 18 explicit missing-key cases currently yield no specific labels in identifiers/plaintext/JSON; IPv6, MAC, reserved phone and DB-URI-only shapes also lack value matches; coordinate fields are named hints only.

limits: No new subtype implemented by this review; only the explicitly authorized reconcile compatibility guard changed product code.
Synthetic failures prove implementation gaps, not AIDev prevalence. The real probe is owned by another agent.
All proposed labels remain static low-confidence candidates requiring human/context review; no protected attribute inferred about an actual person.
The cited DPV community vocabulary is not a W3C Standard; NIST/OIDC provide technical examples, not case-specific legal determinations.
